q: Quantum key distribution (BB84 protocol) achieves information-theoretic security because any eavesdropper Eve disturbs the channel with detectable error rate. The key reconciliation and privacy amplification step reduces the key to length approximately:
opts: n bits regardless of error rate
n[1 − H_b(e)] bits where e is the quantum bit error rate and H_b is binary entropy
exp: After error correction and privacy amplification, the secret key length is ≈ n[1 − H_b(e) − H_b(e_z)] ≈ n[1 − 2H_b(e)] in the symmetric case. At error rate e ≥ 11% (for BB84), the key rate drops to zero—above this threshold, no secure key can be extracted.
